Series::TraverseAccessor::find_btw¶

Back to Series::TraverseAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TraverseMatch Series::TraverseAccessor::find_btw(double lo, double hi,
                                               bool inclusive = true) const;
TraverseMatch Series::TraverseAccessor::find_btw(const Series& lo, const Series& hi,
                                               bool inclusive = true) const;

TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_btw(double lo, double hi,
                                            bool inclusive = true) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_btw(const Series& lo, const Series& hi,
                                            bool inclusive = true) const;

What It Does¶

find_btw(lo, hi) returns the coordinates of every position whose value falls inside the band between lo and hi. It is find_all with a two-sided mask built for you:

  • inclusive = true (default): value >= lo && value <= hi

  • inclusive = false: value > lo && value < hi

Both bounds accept either a scalar or a broadcast peer Series, so the band can vary by row, column, or position — for example “values within one standard deviation of each row’s mean.”

find_btw is also the practical way to match a computed value with tolerance: comparisons produced by arithmetic rarely satisfy exact find_eq, but a narrow find_btw(target - eps, target + eps) band does.

Parameters¶

lo (double or const Series&)

The lower bound.

hi (double or const Series&)

The upper bound.

inclusive (bool, default true)

true includes the endpoints; false excludes both. There is no one-sided option — for that use find_ge or find_le.

Returns¶

TraverseMatch Row-major coordinates and matched values of the in-band positions. K can be 0.

Gradient¶

Coordinates carry no gradient. match.values() and match.select_from(other) are differentiable gathers.

Examples¶

Example 1. An inclusive band keeps both endpoints.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto band = grid.traverse.find_btw(4.0, 8.0);

std::cout << "count=" << band.count() << "\n";
std::cout << band.coords();
std::cout << band.values();

Output¶

count=5
pluss::Series(shape=[5,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=10, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 1],
  [0, 2],
  [1, 2],
  [2, 0],
  [2, 2]]
pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[4, 7, 6, 8, 5]

The endpoints 4 (row 0, column 1) and 8 (row 2, column 0) are both in the result.

Example 2. The same band, exclusive, drops the endpoints.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto strict = grid.traverse.find_btw(4.0, 8.0, /*inclusive=*/false);

std::cout << "count=" << strict.count() << "\n";
std::cout << strict.values();

Output¶

count=3
pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[7, 6, 5]

4 and 8 are gone; only 7, 6, 5 remain strictly between.

Example 3. Tolerance matching for a computed value.

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto approx_seven = grid.traverse.find_btw(7.0 - 1e-9, 7.0 + 1e-9);

std::cout << "count=" << approx_seven.count() << "\n";
std::cout << approx_seven.coords();

Output¶

count=1
pluss::Series(shape=[1,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 2]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • inclusive toggles both endpoints together; there is no per-side control.

  • For a one-sided bound use find_ge or find_le.

  • Series bounds must broadcast to the traversed shape.

  • An empty band (lo > hi) simply produces count() == 0.

  • Coordinates are non-differentiable; values() and select_from() are.

Summary¶

find_btw(lo, hi [, inclusive]) finds every position inside a band:

  • inclusive default keeps endpoints; pass false to exclude both

  • scalar or broadcast-Series bounds

  • the tolerance-friendly alternative to find_eq

See Also¶

  • find_ge / find_le: one-sided bounds.

  • find_eq: exact match; find_btw with a narrow band adds tolerance.

  • find_all: supply an arbitrary two-sided mask.

  • TraverseMatch: the result object.
